Einstein summation

Source: R/numpy_einsum.R
jnp_einsum.Rd

Ports of jnp.einsum and jnp.einsum_path. Subscripts follow NumPy ("ij,jk->ik", implicit output, ... broadcasting); the interleaved form jnp_einsum(x, c(0, 1), y, c(1, 2), c(0, 2)) is also accepted (sublists may be lists containing ellipsis). Contractions are planned pairwise as in opt_einsum: optimize = "auto" (optimal for up to four operands, greedy beyond), TRUE (optimal), "optimal", "greedy", FALSE (left to right) or an explicit path (a list of 0-based index pairs).

Usage

jnp_einsum(
  subscripts,
  ...,
  out = NULL,
  optimize = "auto",
  precision = NULL,
  preferred_element_type = NULL
)

jnp_einsum_path(subscripts, ..., optimize = "auto")

Arguments

subscripts

Subscript string (or the first operand of the interleaved form).

...

Operands (and sublists in the interleaved form).

out

Not supported.

optimize

Path optimization (see Details).

precision

Optional precision for the dot products.

preferred_element_type

Optional accumulation and result dtype.

Value

jnp_einsum returns an array. jnp_einsum_path returns a list of two elements: the path (a list of 0-based integer vectors) and a printable summary string.
